steps.text: Mix flour, water, eggs, salt, and baking powder in a bowl until blended.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Place part of the dough into a spaetzle press or potato ricer. Press dough into boiling water; cook and stir until pasta floats, about 2 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon and rinse with water; repeat with remaining dough.

raw_recipe.headline: Papa Oriold's Spaetzle
raw_recipe.description: With only 5 ingredients and about 15 minutes, you can make these authentic little German noodles as a great addition to soup or your favorite sauce.
raw_recipe.name: Papa Oriold's Spaetzle

review.reviewBody:
This is exactly the taste I was looking for. Paired it with my Traditional Sauerbraten for a home run.
If you don't have a press or ricer, the (traditional) way my Grandmother did it was to put the dough on a cutting board and then "slice" small pieces into the boiling water. It's hard to explain, but basically she would cut about a finger's size of dough and scrape it to the edge of the cutting board. Works great with this recipe!

Quick and great. I use a plastic bag, nip the end and then squeeze it out and use a scissors to cut the length I want! Good with pot roast, sauerbraten, or in place of dumplings in chicken and dumplings!
That tiny bit of baking powder is a game changer. These were lighter and fluffier than any dumpling I have ever had. I used this for drop spoon dumplings. Super good.

I used this recipe but not the method to drop the dough into the boiling water. I saw a video where they use a metal strainer and ladle. Simply use the bottom of the ladle by rubbing the mixture through the holes while it is above the pot of boiling water. The video is on YouTube. Enjoy

I made these with sauerbraten for Christmas. They turned out great. I had to add water though to make the dough thin enough to press through a colander. I think I'll try the plastic bag and scissors next time!

At the last minute I changed this recipe from my usual egg and flour recipe. My German grandmother taught me how to make many types of noodles when I was a teen over 50 years ago. Spatzle though is the only dumpling that stands up to sauerbraten and the thick gravy I make to accompany this dish. This time I decided to check out different recipes and found this one. I grabbed fizzy water from my daughter refrig. Oh my heaven. The spatzle was light but thick and strong. My 7 year old grandson was thrilled wit the recipe. Tomorrow I will have to make another full recipe.
Make it for chicken and "dumplings" instead of the "American dumplings" Love the taste.
Son never eats noodles, put cheese and butter on his, I made pork and gravy with these and was thrilled. Reminded me of a German friend who used to make these... Super easy
Just like my mother made. Been looking for this recipe for a long time.
The liquid (water and eggs) to flour ratio is off. I had to keep adding more and more flour to get it to the correct consistency. I will not be using this recipe again.

I followed this recipe to the letter and, having made spaetzle many times in the past, the batter seemed to be a bit too soft. I probably should have added more flour when I saw the results but I forged ahead and, using a spaetzle press my wife rescued from the trash when we were stationed in Germany, ended up with a large portion of smallish noodles that tasted okay. I certainly wouldn’t be using this recipe for kaese spaetzle or with a hearty mushroom white sauce.
This is a great easy spaetzle recipe
This recipe seems very good. I am looking to make spaetzle and will most likely use this recipe!
I didn't have a spätzle press or a river so I tried to drop in small globs off a spoon and I found they were really watery. I'm not sure what happened.
This is a great receipt! My family enjoys spaetzle with Swiss cheese and Caramelized onions! My husband could eat the whole dish if I'd let him.

My great grandmother made a soup called "ripple soup" it had the same noodles. It was made with beef and a beef bone. Wonderful. I can't believe someone gave this a bad rating saying it has no flavor. It's a pasta!! I drop mine in small pinches to boiling stock. Amazing
I made this tonight. Don't expect any flavor taste just like it should a dough ball boiled in water lol. I won't make it again.
